title: UK cyber force commander says it is running offensive cyber operations against Russia, China, Iran and North Korea
date_note: Published November 20 by Sky News; interview given around the opening of the National Cyber Force headquarters.
summary: In a Sky News interview, General Sir Rob Magowan, who commands the UK's Cyber & Specialist Operations Command, said the National Cyber Force is conducting offensive cyber operations, answering "Absolutely" when asked. He named Russia, China, Iran and North Korea as threats and said there would be a cost to them. He called the activity highly classified and gave no specifics.
plain: A senior UK military commander said publicly that Britain is carrying out offensive cyber operations against four rival states.
exec: A public statement of UK offensive cyber activity signals a more open deterrence stance toward these four states.
impact: Policy statement only; no operations or effects were described.

validation.note: Sky News report (Deborah Haynes) as republished by Manx Radio; one reporting chain, no government release read.
